Pre-checkpoint mutation, actor, expiry/revocation and stale-history negatives reject before migration calls; post-checkpoint revocation retains in-flight effects and blocks later permits. This is a harness model, not certified platform authorization.
Each required parser/runtime fixture has independent 19c/21c evidence; driver return success cannot hide invalid or unobserved objects.
Observed execution counts are A=2/B=4 then both zero; no fake receipt seeding or changed-checksum repair.
All mandatory fault cases retain actual observations and block unproven replay; logical rewind is never reported as an actual Oracle restore.
All security/license/offline cells pass with evidence or remain explicitly BLOCKED; mandatory dependency rights and secrecy are hard gates.
A signed/reviewed decision says GO only when every mandatory applicable cell passes; otherwise CONDITIONAL GO for further probes or NO-GO with exact blockers.
Approved workspace builds its empty API/worker/domain packages and contract fixtures; no production deployment.
Cross-org FK and invalid archive negatives fail transactionally; seeded fixture organizations/projects/environments remain isolated.
Denied and successful actions retain authenticated actor/resource/time/intent; altered blobs are rejected and worker deletion loses no evidence.
Cross-language canonical hashes agree; RETURNED/INVALID and UNKNOWN receipt examples never become VERIFIED_SUCCESS.
Supported metadata upgrades preserve immutable identities and audit/artifacts; incompatible versions fail readiness before claims.
Wrong PDB/trust/scope, user-supplied DSNs and API writer-secret reads fail before migrations.
Same alias target shares mutex identity; other PDB/owner differs; schema labels cannot downgrade an environment.
Repeated discovery yields two stable application owners; invisible diagnostics do not become VALID or authorize writes.
A metadata fixture with 500 schema references retains shared endpoint rows without duplicate credentials; runtime two-project isolation passes.
Old-generation intent is unusable even when names/DBID match; quarantine is durable and auditable.
Core inventory supports representative estate management without alias duplication, unauthorized count disclosure or stale-plan execution.
Grouped estate data is correctly authorized and read-only; no duplicate physical resource model.
Only the bound repository/folder can ingest; read failures are sanitized and configuration changes invalidate relevant intents.
A branch move cannot alter retained bytes; ambiguous short IDs fail and unsupported object formats fail explicitly.
All five fixture migrations ingest together; V001/V1 duplicate fails and V2 precedes V10 with reproducible raw hashes.
A malformed later file blocks the entire release before effects; manifest identity changes with execution-affecting content and works while Git is offline.
A=1..3/B=1 yields pending 2/4; changed V002 and unobserved history block; zero-pending intent remains reviewable.
Core planning keeps identical source semantics across providers and stages and does not re-run baseline/adopted versions.
Unauthenticated/forged/revoked actors cannot read resources or approve; no caller-supplied actor ID becomes trusted.
Direct API, CLI and guessed cross-project IDs fail consistently; revocation denies new actions and requester cannot gain execution permission.
Exact SQL/target/options/history are previewable; all mutation/self-approval/expiry negatives deny and decisions remain auditable.
Same body/key returns same job; conflicts and revocations block; approver role alone cannot dispatch and worker receives no caller-supplied SQL.
Current-authority mutation and permit commit have an explicit serialized order; revocation never promises an already-permitted Oracle call is recalled.
Logout, credential/session expiry and removal deny further approval/admission without waiting for a UI refresh.
Guided resubmission cannot reuse old decisions or erase contributors; history remains immutable.
Bootstrap refuses populated unmanaged or wrong-generation targets; local receipt uniqueness is independent of central history.
Observer history reads succeed only within authorized target scope; missing grants block planning, and the API cannot resolve owner/bootstrap credentials.
Alias/session contention, DDL commit and paused-lease probes show no concurrent target writes.
Duplicate delivery cannot duplicate SQL; changed snapshot invalidates approval; zero-pending run retains audit and zero-call proof.
Pre-checkpoint revocation denies SQL; post-checkpoint revocation stops future permits and truthfully retains in-flight/unknown effects.
Schema/data effects match approved bytes; failures preserve last acknowledged calls and four outcome axes; target receipt cannot precede required file validation.
Valid specification/invalid body, missing object and failed postcheck never become VERIFIED_SUCCESS; successful receipts/effects remain truthful.
500 schema metadata entries do not open 500 idle writer sessions; configuration cannot bypass target serialization.
No ledger absence proves no effect; unknown admission prevents replay and missing authorization is never fabricated.
Crash, SIGTERM and lease expiry leave honest unresolved state; read-only incident inspection works with protected evidence.
No automatic or operator reset-to-pending exists; unknown DDL and forged recovery approval cannot run.
No ordinary APPLIED fabrication or checksum editing; lower unknown version blocks correction until authorized resolution; baseline/adoption retain different provenance.
Both-direction actual restore exercises prove no automatic queued replay; logical rewind tests alone cannot close this production gate.
CLI/API expose the same authorized plan and statement digest; approved actor cannot be supplied as an unauthenticated flag.
A user can reconstruct a completed, invalid and ambiguous run from persisted facts; driver success never hides compiler errors.
Every WS feature acceptance and sixteen-outcome checklist passes on both versions; harness results do not substitute for this integrated regression.
Presentation does not alter approval/admission semantics and omitted views do not block safe core operation.
Every applicable Core action and negative cross-project/missing-approval/restore-hold path passes on actual modules.
Actual GitLab version/API compatibility and branch-move/outage negatives pass; a CI caller cannot approve or obtain writer secrets.
Missing/failed/invalid/unknown UAT blocks PROD admission; no execution against actual production during implementation acceptance.
No privileged SCC/external egress needed; API cannot read writer secrets; dependency outage changes readiness without liveness restart loops.
Every shipped dependency has provenance/rights/hash; air-gapped install/update succeeds without proprietary required components.
Authorized recipients can independently validate exported evidence with a reviewed OSS offline tool; no proprietary service dependency.
Another developer can reproduce the bounded WS process topology and input checks from a fresh checkout.
All negative permission/secret/transport tests pass and exact remaining risks have explicit operating owners.
Required SQL hashes/decisions/compiler/recovery evidence survives pods, retention operations and restored metadata; no secret backup leakage.
Documented required capacity and agreed p95/session budgets pass with actual target workload evidence; synthetic metadata alone cannot certify estate execution scale.
Recipient can match approved bytes to recorded execution/target; modified or missing evidence fails verification and cross-project export is denied.
Production readiness is supported by actual integrated evidence, not research or WP0 alone; explicit deployment authorization remains separate.
All sixteen outcomes and applicable WS invariants have actual module evidence; only named DEV capabilities are accepted.
A reproducible local command starts the API, web application, and PostgreSQL-backed metadata store.
Projects, environments, and connection profiles persist; connection secrets never appear in API responses or logs.
A Git migration release can be imported, parsed, validated, and displayed with source references.
The application generates a pending-change plan with approval and rejection transitions and audit history.
Migration history records NOT_EXECUTED when no authorized database execution occurs; no success is fabricated.
A project can be archived persistently and its archived state is visible in project list and detail responses.
Archived projects reject new environments, connection profiles, Git releases, and migration plans with a stable conflict response.
Existing project details, audit events, and migration history remain readable after archival.

The reproducible development CLI uses Node's native parseArgs for one to eight repeatable --repository PATH options, registers existing local Git directories, and displays only repository IDs and names.
Invalid flags, URLs, and non-repository paths are rejected before PostgreSQL or Docker startup with fixed errors that do not disclose supplied paths.

Registration never clones, fetches, or resolves provider credentials; custom releases use the existing parser with an immutable resolved commit, database execution remains NOT_EXECUTED, and no Oracle behavior is claimed.
A project can persist and display its source binding using an allowlisted repository ID and migration folder; API and web views never expose repository paths or credentials.
Imports reject an unbound project or repository/folder mismatch before Git or parser work begins.
Archived projects reject source-binding changes while existing releases, plans, audit history, and migration history remain readable with execution state NOT_EXECUTED.
Authenticated plan-decision rejections for role, author, and terminal-state conflicts record a fixed denial reason and server actor/resource metadata without changing the plan or migration history.
Malformed and unauthenticated requests cannot persist arbitrary request data; archived projects reject review requests without appending new project audit events.
The web audit view displays denied decisions; existing approval/rejection transitions remain terminal and all migration execution states remain NOT_EXECUTED.
Authenticated local developers and approvers can append bounded plain-text comments to pending plans; the server supplies actor/time and binds each comment to its organization, project and plan.
The review UI displays the persisted thread; malformed, missing-plan, terminal-plan and archived-project writes are denied, while existing comments remain readable.
Comments cannot attach files or change migration bytes, plan decisions or history; execution remains NOT_EXECUTED and no full catalog or Oracle acceptance is claimed.

Authenticated plan reviews display terminal decision reason, server timestamp and reviewer identity; new decisions snapshot the configured reviewer name, while historical records retain their stored actor ID fallback.

Approval and rejection records remain scoped, readable after archival and application restart, and render arbitrary reason text safely without changing decision transitions, plan content, comments or migration history.
Unauthorized reads and invalid or spoofed decision writes remain denied; this bounded provenance view does not certify project transfer, full catalog audit or Oracle execution.
